definition_en: a feeling from the body, the meaning of something, good judgment, or to become aware of something
core_image: 指尖轻轻碰到杯壁，热度顺着皮肤传上来
scene: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 sensed 是「感觉到」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。

senses.title: Body feeling
senses.definition: a feeling produced by the senses
senses.definitionCN: 由感官产生的感觉
senses.example: She felt a sense of warmth from the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 她从杯子上感到一阵暖意。
senses.why: This is the basic sensory sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的感官义。

senses.title: Meaning
senses.definition: the meaning that words or actions carry
senses.definitionCN: 词语或行为所承载的意义
senses.example: I cannot make sense of this sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 我弄不懂这个句子的意思。
senses.why: Meaning is what the mind grasps.
senses.whyCN: 意义是心智所把握的东西。

senses.title: Good judgment
senses.definition: practical good judgment
senses.definitionCN: 实际而良好的判断力
senses.example: It is common sense to lock the door.
senses.why: The mind's sense becomes sound judgment.
senses.whyCN: 心智的感觉变成健全的判断。

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become aware of something without being told
senses.definitionCN: 未经告知而察觉到某事
senses.example: She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of perceiving.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为感知的动作。

intro.en: Sense comes from Latin sentire, to feel, through Latin sensus, a feeling.
intro.cn: sense 出自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），经拉丁语 sensus（感觉）而来。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or perceive.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或察觉。

items.en: Sensus named a feeling or meaning.
items.cn: sensus 指感觉或意义。

items.en: Sens carried both feeling and meaning.
items.cn: sens 兼具感觉与意义。

items.en: Sense added the idea of good judgment.
items.cn: sense 增加了良好判断之义。

items.en: Make sense became a common phrase.
items.cn: make sense 成为常用短语。

note.en: Sense is compared with similar-looking words and with words for feeling and meaning.
note.cn: 把 sense 与形近词以及表示感觉和意义的词作比较。

entries.definition: from a past time until now

normalIntro.en: Sense covers what the body feels, what words mean, and what the mind judges.
normalIntro.cn: sense 涵盖身体所感、词语所表与心智所判。

normal.en: We have five senses.
A sentence must make sense.
Common sense is judgment without special training.
normal.cn: 常识是无需专门训练的判断力。

normal.en: She sensed danger before she saw it.
normal.cn: 她在看见危险之前就察觉到了。

normal.en: In a sense, both answers are right.
normal.cn: 在某种意义上，两个答案都对。

abstract.en: Meaning is the shape a feeling takes when it is shared.
abstract.cn: 意义是感觉被分享时呈现的形状。

abstract.en: Good judgment is feeling trained by experience.
abstract.cn: 良好的判断力是被经验训练过的感觉。

abstract.en: We notice most what we have learned to sense.
abstract.cn: 我们最容易察觉自己学会去感受的东西。

examples.en: She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
examples.cn: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。

examples.en: I cannot make sense of this sentence.
examples.cn: 我弄不懂这个句子的意思。

examples.en: It is common sense to lock the door.

dict_mnemonic.text: sense 出自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），本义「感官所感」，后扩展为意义、判断力与察觉。

root: 源自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），核心义「感知与领会」。

sensesIntro.en: Sense means a body feeling, a meaning, good judgment, or the act of perceiving.
sensesIntro.cn: sense 意为身体感觉、意义、理智或察觉。

core.en: The mind and body taking in what is there.
core.cn: 身心对眼前之物的接收。

branches.en: Warmth, smell, or sound received by the body.
branches.cn: 身体接收到的热、气味或声音。

branches.en: What a sentence or action means.
branches.cn: 句子或行为所表达的意思。

branches.en: Practical judgment about daily life.
branches.cn: 关于日常生活的实际判断。

branches.en: Noticing something before being told.
branches.cn: 在被告知之前就注意到某事。

branches.en: Feeling and noticing are two sides of one act.
branches.cn: 感受与察觉是同一动作的两面。

intro.en: Sense belongs to the Latin sentire family of feeling and perceiving.
intro.cn: sense 属于拉丁语 sentire（感觉）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire and sensus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire 与 sensus 是历史词根。

items.example: He has a sense of duty.

items.exampleCN: 这个设备正在感应运动。

items.example: The cold caused a burning sensation.

definition_en: a group of words that expresses a complete idea, a punishment given by a court, or to order a punishment
core_image: 纸上写着一行完整的字，末尾落下一个句点
scene: 他写了一个很长的句子。He wrote a very long sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 sentence 是「句子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他写了一个很长的句子。

senses.title: Group of words
senses.definition: a group of words that expresses a complete thought
senses.definitionCN: 表达完整思想的一组词
senses.example: He wrote a very long sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他写了一个很长的句子。
senses.why: This is the grammar sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是语法义。

senses.title: Court punishment
senses.definition: a punishment ordered by a court
senses.definitionCN: 法庭判处的惩罚
senses.example: The judge gave him a light sentence.
senses.why: A court's judgment is also called a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的判断也叫 sentence。

senses.title: To order punishment
senses.definition: to order a punishment in court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上判处惩罚
senses.example: The court sentenced him to two years.
senses.why: The noun becomes the judge's action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为法官的动作。

intro.en: Sentence comes from Latin sententia, an opinion or judgment, from sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: sentence 出自拉丁语 sententia（意见、判断），源于 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or think.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或思考。

items.en: Sententia meant an opinion or judgment.
items.cn: sententia 意为意见或判断。

items.en: Old French sentence kept the judgment sense.
items.cn: 古法语 sentence 保留了判断义。

items.en: English sentence meant opinion or legal judgment.
items.cn: 英语 sentence 意为意见或法律判决。

items.en: The grammar sense became dominant.
items.cn: 语法义后来占据主导。

note.en: Sentence is compared with similar-looking words and with grammar and law words.
note.cn: 把 sentence 与形近词以及语法、法律类词作比较。

entries.definition: a part of a sentence with a verb

normalIntro.en: Sentence is a complete thought in words, and also a court's judgment.
normalIntro.cn: sentence 是用词语表达的完整思想，也是法庭的判决。

normal.en: A sentence begins with a capital letter.
A topic sentence states the main idea.
A life sentence lasts many years.
The judge passed sentence at noon.
Sentence and sentiment share a root.

abstract.en: A sentence closes a thought the way a door closes a room.
abstract.cn: 句子结束一个思想，就像门关上一个房间。

abstract.en: Judgment and grammar both put things in order.
abstract.cn: 判决与语法都在给事物排定秩序。

abstract.en: The same word can hold a thought or a punishment.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能装思想，也能装惩罚。

examples.en: He wrote a very long sentence.
examples.cn: 他写了一个很长的句子。

examples.en: The judge gave him a light sentence.
The court sentenced him to two years.

dict_mnemonic.text: sentence 出自拉丁语 sententia（意见、判断），源于 sentire（感觉、思考），本义「所想的判断」，后兼指语法句子与法庭判决。

root: 源自拉丁语 sententia（判断、意见），出自 sentire（感觉、思考），核心义「完整表达出的判断」。

sensesIntro.en: Sentence means a complete group of words, a court's punishment, or to order that punishment.
sensesIntro.cn: sentence 意为完整的句子、法庭判决或宣判。

core.en: A complete judgment, in words or in law.
core.cn: 用言语或法律作出的完整判断。

branches.en: Words closing into one complete idea.
branches.cn: 收束成一个完整思想的词语。

branches.en: A punishment declared by a court.
The act of declaring that punishment.
Grammar and law both close a matter.
branches.cn: 语法与法律都在了结一件事。

branches.en: The ruling and the saying of it share a name.
branches.cn: 判决与宣判共用一个名称。

intro.en: Sentence belongs to the Latin sentire family of feeling and judging.
intro.cn: sentence 属于拉丁语 sentire（感觉、判断）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sententia and sentire are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sententia 与 sentire 是历史词根。

items.meaning: a complete word group or judgment

items.example: He was sentenced to a fine.

items.meaning: the act of giving a sentence

items.exampleCN: 他说教式的语气让他们厌烦。

definition_zh: 分开的；单独的；分开；分离
definition_en: not joined together, existing on its own, to divide things, or to move apart
core_image: 一条线把一张纸从中间裁开，两半各自落到桌上
scene: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。The teacher separated the students into different groups.
sceneCN: 这里 separated 是「分开」（第 3 个义项）；句意：老师把学生分成不同的小组。

senses.title: Not joined
senses.definition: not joined or connected to something else
senses.definitionCN: 没有与其他事物连在一起
senses.example: The twins sleep in separate beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎睡在不同的床上。
senses.why: This is the basic adjective sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的形容词义。

senses.title: On its own
senses.definition: existing or used on its own
senses.definitionCN: 独立存在或单独使用
senses.example: Each room has a separate entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 每个房间都有单独的入口。
senses.why: Being apart makes something distinct.
senses.whyCN: 彼此分开使事物各自独立。

senses.title: To divide
senses.definition: to divide people or things into groups
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物分成组
senses.example: The teacher separated the students into different groups.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。
senses.why: The adjective turns into the act of dividing.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为分开的动作。

senses.title: To move apart
senses.definition: to move apart or stop living together
senses.definitionCN: 彼此离开或不再共同生活
senses.example: The couple separated last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻去年春天分居了。
senses.why: People and paths can separate too.
senses.whyCN: 人与道路也可以分离。

intro.en: Separate comes from Latin separare, from se-, apart, and parare, to prepare.
intro.cn: separate 出自拉丁语 separare，由 se-（分开）与 parare（准备）构成。

items.en: Se- meant apart.
items.cn: se- 意为分开。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare or arrange.
items.cn: parare 意为准备或安排。

items.en: Separare meant to set apart.
items.cn: separare 意为使分开。

items.en: English separate covered both the adjective and the verb.
items.cn: 英语 separate 兼作形容词与动词。

items.en: The spelling kept one form for both uses.
items.cn: 拼写保留了两种词性共用的一个形式。

note.en: Separate is compared with similar-looking words and with words for dividing.
note.cn: 把 separate 与形近词以及表示分开的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Separate means set apart, whether as an adjective or an action.
normalIntro.cn: separate 意为使分开，无论作形容词还是动词。

normal.en: The adjective ends with a soft sound.
normal.cn: 形容词形式的结尾发音较轻。

normal.en: The verb ends with the sound of ate.
normal.cn: 动词形式的结尾读作 ate 的音。

normal.en: Separate the white clothes from the dark.
normal.cn: 把浅色衣服与深色衣服分开。

normal.en: They keep separate accounts.
The couple separated after ten years.
normal.cn: 这对夫妻十年后分居了。

abstract.en: To name a thing is to set it apart.
abstract.cn: 给事物命名，就是把它区分出来。

abstract.en: Some things grow stronger when kept apart.
abstract.cn: 有些事物分开后反而更强。

abstract.en: A line divides the page but joins the story.
abstract.cn: 一条线分开纸页，却连起故事。

examples.en: The teacher separated the students into different groups.
examples.cn: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。

examples.en: Each room has a separate entrance.
examples.cn: 每个房间都有单独的入口。

examples.en: The couple separated last spring.
examples.cn: 这对夫妻去年春天分居了。

dict_mnemonic.text: separate 出自拉丁语 separare（使分开），由 se-（分开）与 parare（安排）构成，本义「分别安置」，兼作形容词与动词。

root: 源自拉丁语 separare，由 se-（分开）与 parare（安排）构成，核心义「分别安置」。

sensesIntro.en: Separate means not joined, existing alone, to divide, or to move apart.
sensesIntro.cn: separate 意为分开的、单独的、分开或分离。

core.en: Things set apart from one another.
core.cn: 彼此被分开的事物。

branches.en: Two things no longer joined.
One thing standing on its own.
The act of dividing a group.
branches.cn: 把一个群体分开的动作。

branches.en: Two people or paths moving apart.
branches.cn: 两个人或两条路彼此远离。

branches.en: Being apart and making apart share one word.
branches.cn: 分开的状态与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Separate belongs to the Latin parare family of preparing and arranging.
intro.cn: separate 属于拉丁语 parare（准备、安排）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin separare and parare are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 separare 与 parare 是历史词根。

items.example: The filter is separating the oil.

definition_zh: 严肃的；严重的；认真的；重大的
definition_en: not joking, very bad or dangerous, sincere about something, or important enough to need attention
core_image: 病房门上的灯亮着，走廊里的人都不再说话
scene: 这是一起严重的交通事故。This is a serious traffic accident.
sceneCN: 这里 serious 是「严重的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这是一起严重的交通事故。

senses.title: Not joking
senses.definition: not joking or laughing
senses.definitionCN: 不开玩笑或不带笑意
senses.example: Her face was serious during the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会时她的表情很严肃。
senses.why: This is the basic manner sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的神情义。

senses.title: Very bad
senses.definition: very bad or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 非常糟糕或危险
senses.example: This is a serious traffic accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一起严重的交通事故。
senses.why: A serious matter can cause real harm.
senses.whyCN: 严重的事会造成真正的伤害。

senses.title: Sincere
senses.definition: sincere and in earnest about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事真诚而认真
senses.example: He is serious about learning Chinese.
senses.why: A serious person means what they say.
senses.whyCN: 认真的人言出必真。

senses.title: Important
senses.definition: important enough to need careful attention
senses.definitionCN: 重要到需要认真对待
senses.example: We face a serious decision.
senses.exampleCN: 我们面临一个重大决定。
senses.why: Importance gives a matter weight.
senses.whyCN: 重要性赋予一件事分量。

intro.en: Serious comes from Latin serius, weighty or grave.
intro.cn: serious 出自拉丁语 serius（有分量的、严肃的）。

items.en: Serius meant weighty or grave.
items.cn: serius 意为有分量的、严肃的。

items.en: Seriosus described a serious manner.
items.cn: seriosus 形容严肃的举止。

items.en: Old French serieux kept the grave sense.
items.cn: 古法语 serieux 保留了严肃义。

items.en: English serious covered manner and importance.
items.cn: 英语 serious 兼指神情与重要性。

items.en: It also names grave problems and injuries.
items.cn: 它也用来形容严重的问题与伤势。

note.en: Serious is compared with similar-looking words and with words for gravity.
note.cn: 把 serious 与形近词以及表示严重的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Serious means heavy in manner, in harm, or in importance.
normalIntro.cn: serious 意为神情、危害或重要性上的沉重。

normal.en: A serious face shows no joke.
A serious injury needs a doctor.
She is serious about her studies.
The adverb is seriously.
The noun is seriousness.

abstract.en: Weight is the image behind every sense of serious.
abstract.cn: 沉重是 serious 每个义项背后的意象。

abstract.en: What matters asks for our full attention.
abstract.cn: 重要之事要求我们全神贯注。

abstract.en: To be earnest is to mean what one says.
abstract.cn: 认真就是言出必真。

examples.en: This is a serious traffic accident.
examples.cn: 这是一起严重的交通事故。

examples.en: He is serious about learning Chinese.
We face a serious decision.
examples.cn: 我们面临一个重大决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: serious 出自拉丁语 serius（有分量的），本义「沉重的」，后指神情严肃、情况严重、态度认真与事关重大。

root: 源自拉丁语 serius（有分量的、严肃的），核心义「沉重而有分量」。

sensesIntro.en: Serious means not joking, very bad, sincere, or important.
sensesIntro.cn: serious 意为严肃的、严重的、认真的或重大的。

core.en: Weight that demands attention.
core.cn: 需要被认真对待的分量。

branches.en: A face without a joke.
Harm that is hard to undo.
Sincerity in what one does.
A choice with large consequences.
Harm and importance both carry weight.
branches.cn: 危害与重要性都带着分量。

intro.en: Serious belongs to the Latin serius family of weight and gravity.
intro.cn: serious 属于拉丁语 serius（沉重）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin serius is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serius 是历史词根。

items.example: He understood the seriousness of it.
The hall was full of solemnity.
The severity of the pain shocked her.

definition_en: a person employed to work in another's household, a public official, or someone who serves
core_image: 旧式厨房里，仆人把托盘端得又稳又平
scene: 老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。The old servant worked for the family for thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里 servant 是「仆人」（第 1 个义项）；句意：老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。

senses.title: Household worker
senses.definition: a person employed to work in a household
senses.definitionCN: 受雇在家庭中工作的人
senses.example: The old servant worked for the family for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。
senses.why: This is the traditional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是传统义。

senses.title: Public official
senses.definition: a person who works for the state or public
senses.definitionCN: 为国家或公众工作的人
senses.example: Civil servants serve the public.
senses.why: Serving expands from a home to a state.
senses.whyCN: 服务从家庭扩展到国家。

senses.title: One who serves
senses.definition: a person who serves a cause or an employer
senses.definitionCN: 为事业或雇主服务的人
senses.example: He was a faithful servant of the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这项事业的忠实服务者。
senses.why: The core idea is service itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心观念是服务本身。

intro.en: Servant comes from Old French servant, from servir, from Latin servire, to serve.
intro.cn: servant 出自古法语 servant，源于 servir，再追溯到拉丁语 servire（服务）。

items.en: Servire meant to serve.
items.cn: servire 意为服务。

items.en: Serviens meant serving.
items.cn: serviens 意为服务的。

items.en: Servant named one who serves.
items.cn: servant 指服务的人。

items.en: English servant named household workers.
items.cn: 英语 servant 指家庭佣人。

items.en: Civil servant names a public official.
items.cn: civil servant 指公务员。

note.en: Servant is compared with similar-looking words and with words for people who serve.
note.cn: 把 servant 与形近词以及表示服务者的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who helps in a place

normalIntro.en: A servant is anyone whose work is to serve, at home or in public office.
normalIntro.cn: servant 是以服务为业的人，无论在家中还是公共岗位。

normal.en: Servant comes from the Latin verb to serve.
normal.cn: servant 出自拉丁语中表示服务的动词。

normal.en: A civil servant works for the state.
The plural is servants.
A servant carries out another's orders.
Servant and service share a root.

abstract.en: To serve is to put another's need before one's own.
abstract.cn: 服务就是把他人的需要放在自己之前。

abstract.en: The word reminds us who public power belongs to.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们公共权力属于谁。

abstract.en: Dignity belongs to the work, not the title.
abstract.cn: 尊严属于工作本身，而非头衔。

examples.en: The old servant worked for the family for thirty years.
examples.cn: 老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。

examples.en: Civil servants serve the public.
He was a faithful servant of the cause.
examples.cn: 他是这项事业的忠实服务者。

dict_mnemonic.text: servant 出自古法语 servant，源于拉丁语 servire（服务），本义「服务的人」，后兼指家仆、公务员与事业的服务者。

root: 源自拉丁语 servire（服务），核心义「以服务为业的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Servant means a household worker, a public official, or a person who serves a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: servant 意为仆人、公务员或服务者。

core.en: A person whose role is to serve.
core.cn: 以服务为角色的人。

branches.en: A worker inside a household.
A worker inside the state.
A person devoted to a cause.
Home and state both employ servants.
branches.cn: 家庭与国家都雇用服务者。

branches.en: Public duty and personal devotion meet.
branches.cn: 公共职责与个人忠诚在此相遇。

intro.en: Servant belongs to the Latin servire family of service.
intro.cn: servant 属于拉丁语 servire（服务）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin servire and servus are the historical base.

items.example: The servants kept the house clean.

items.exampleCN: 他奴性的态度让她厌烦。

items.meaning: the state of being a servant

items.exampleCN: 奴性没有为他赢得尊重。

items.meaning: a person or machine that serves

definition_zh: 服务；供应；端上；任职；发球
definition_en: to work for others, to provide food or goods, to hold a position, to spend time in prison, or to start play in tennis
core_image: 餐厅里托盘从厨房稳稳送到桌边，杯口一滴未洒
scene: 这家餐厅供应新鲜的海鲜。This restaurant serves fresh seafood.
sceneCN: 这里 serves 是「供应」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这家餐厅供应新鲜的海鲜。

senses.title: Work for others
senses.definition: to work for a person, group, or cause
senses.definitionCN: 为个人、群体或事业工作
senses.example: She has served the company for ten years.
senses.why: This is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义。

senses.title: Provide food
senses.definition: to provide or put food on the table
senses.definitionCN: 提供食物或把食物端上桌
senses.example: This restaurant serves fresh seafood.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅供应新鲜的海鲜。
senses.why: Serving at table is a concrete kind of service.
senses.whyCN: 在餐桌旁服务是具体的服务。

senses.title: Hold a post
senses.definition: to hold an official position
senses.definitionCN: 担任官方职位
senses.example: He served as mayor for two terms.
senses.why: Public service is service in office.
senses.whyCN: 公共职务是在职位上的服务。

senses.title: Spend time in prison
senses.definition: to spend a period in prison
senses.definitionCN: 在监狱中度过一段时间
senses.example: He served time for theft.
senses.why: A sentence is served as a duty.
senses.whyCN: 刑期作为一种义务被服完。

senses.title: Start play
senses.definition: to begin a point in tennis or a similar game
senses.definitionCN: 在网球等比赛中开始一分
senses.example: She served the first ball.
senses.why: The player puts the ball into play.
senses.whyCN: 球员把球送入比赛。

intro.en: Serve comes from Latin servire, to serve, through Old French servir.
intro.cn: serve 出自拉丁语 servire（服务），经古法语 servir 而来。

items.en: Servire meant to serve or be a slave.
items.cn: servire 意为服务或为奴。

items.en: Servir kept the sense of service.
items.cn: servir 保留了服务义。

items.en: Serve covered work, food, and office.
items.cn: serve 涵盖工作、食物与职位。

items.en: It extended to serving time in prison.
items.cn: 它扩展到在狱中服刑。

items.en: It also names starting play in tennis.
items.cn: 它也指网球中开始发球。

note.en: Serve is compared with similar-looking words and with words for providing.
note.cn: 把 serve 与形近词以及表示提供的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person or machine that serves

normalIntro.en: Serve means to give service, food, office, time, or a first ball.
normalIntro.cn: serve 意为给予服务、食物、职务、刑期或第一个球。

normal.en: Serve food means to put it on the table.
normal.cn: serve food 意为把食物端上桌。

normal.en: Serve as means to act in a role.
normal.cn: serve as 意为担任某个角色。

normal.en: Serve time means to be in prison.
The server brings your order.
In tennis, you serve to start.
normal.cn: 网球中你发球开始一分。

abstract.en: Service turns ability into a gift for others.
abstract.cn: 服务把能力变成给他人的礼物。

abstract.en: A role is a place where one serves.
abstract.cn: 职位是一个人履行服务的位置。

abstract.en: Every beginning in sport is a gift to the opponent.
abstract.cn: 体育中的每次开始都是给对手的一次机会。

examples.en: This restaurant serves fresh seafood.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅供应新鲜的海鲜。

examples.en: She served in the army for five years.
He served time for theft.

dict_mnemonic.text: serve 出自拉丁语 servire（服务），本义「为他人做事」，后扩展为供应食物、担任职务、服刑与发球。

root: 源自拉丁语 servire（服务），核心义「为他人或某项职责效力」。

sensesIntro.en: Serve means to work for others, provide food, hold a post, spend time in prison, or start play.
sensesIntro.cn: serve 意为服务、供应、任职、服刑或发球。

core.en: Giving oneself or something to a purpose.
core.cn: 把自己或某物交付给一个目的。

branches.en: Work given to a person or cause.
branches.cn: 为个人或事业付出的工作。

branches.en: Food placed before guests.
Duty carried out in office.
A sentence carried out in prison.
Both food and a ball are put into play.
branches.cn: 食物与球都被送入各自的场合。

intro.en: Serve belongs to the Latin servire family of service.
intro.cn: serve 属于拉丁语 servire（服务）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin servire and servus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 servire 与 servus 是历史词根。

items.meaning: a person or machine that serves

definition_zh: 服务；公共设施；服役；维修；发球
definition_en: work done for others, a public system such as transport, military duty, the act of maintaining a machine, or a tennis serve
core_image: 清晨的公交车准时停靠，车门打开，乘客依次上车
scene: 顾客对这里的服务非常满意。The customers are very happy with the service.
sceneCN: 这里 service 是「服务」（第 1 个义项）；句意：顾客对这里的服务非常满意。

senses.title: Work for others
senses.definition: work done to help customers or others
senses.definitionCN: 为顾客或他人提供的帮助性工作
senses.example: The customers are very happy with the service.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客对这里的服务非常满意。
senses.why: This is the core modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代核心义。

senses.title: Public system
senses.definition: a system that supplies a public need
senses.definitionCN: 满足公共需求的系统
senses.example: The bus service runs every hour.
senses.why: Service expands from people to systems.
senses.whyCN: 服务从人扩展到系统。

senses.title: Military duty
senses.definition: time spent in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在军队中度过的时间
senses.example: He completed his military service.
senses.why: Serving the state includes military duty.
senses.whyCN: 为国家服务包括服兵役。

senses.title: Maintenance
senses.definition: the act of checking and repairing a machine
senses.definitionCN: 检查与修理机器的行为
senses.example: He took his car in for service.
senses.why: Keeping a machine working is a service.
senses.whyCN: 保持机器运转是一种服务。

senses.title: Tennis serve
senses.definition: the act of starting play by hitting the ball
senses.definitionCN: 击球开始比赛的动作
senses.example: Her service won the game.
senses.exampleCN: 她的发球赢下了这一局。
senses.why: The opening stroke is also named service.
senses.whyCN: 开球动作也叫 service。

intro.en: Service comes from Latin servitium, service or slavery, from servus, slave.
intro.cn: service 出自拉丁语 servitium（服务、奴役），源于 servus（奴隶）。

items.en: Servus meant slave or servant.
items.cn: servus 意为奴隶或仆人。

items.en: Servitium meant service or slavery.
items.cn: servitium 意为服务或奴役。

items.en: Old French servise kept the service sense.
items.cn: 古法语 servise 保留了服务义。

items.en: English service covered work, worship, and duty.
items.cn: 英语 service 涵盖工作、礼拜与职责。

items.en: It extended to public systems and maintenance.
items.cn: 它扩展到公共设施与维修。

note.en: Service is compared with similar-looking words and with words for help and systems.
note.cn: 把 service 与形近词以及表示帮助与系统的词作比较。

entries.definition: a place or system built for a purpose
the work of keeping something in order

normalIntro.en: Service is work done for others, and also the systems and care that keep life running.
normalIntro.cn: service 是为他人做的工作，也是维持生活运转的系统与维护。

normal.en: Good service makes customers return.
normal.cn: 良好的服务让顾客回头。

normal.en: A bus service is a public system.
normal.cn: 公交服务是一种公共系统。

normal.en: Military service is a duty to the state.
A service station repairs cars.
In tennis, service starts the point.

abstract.en: A society is held together by services people rarely see.
abstract.cn: 社会由人们很少看见的服务维系。

abstract.en: Maintenance is service to the future.
abstract.cn: 维护是对未来的服务。

abstract.en: To serve well is to make another's task lighter.
abstract.cn: 好好服务，就是让别人的事情变轻。

examples.en: The customers are very happy with the service.
examples.cn: 顾客对这里的服务非常满意。

examples.en: The bus service runs every hour.
He took his car in for service.

dict_mnemonic.text: service 出自拉丁语 servitium（服务、奴役），源于 servus（奴隶），本义「服务」，后扩展为公共设施、服役、维修与发球。

root: 源自拉丁语 servus（奴隶）与 servitium（服务），核心义「为他人效力」。

sensesIntro.en: Service means work for others, a public system, military duty, maintenance, or a tennis serve.
sensesIntro.cn: service 意为服务、公共设施、服役、维修或发球。

core.en: Work and systems that serve a need.
core.cn: 满足需求的工作与系统。

branches.en: Help given to a customer.
A system that serves the public.
Time given to the armed forces.
Care that keeps a machine running.
Personal help and public systems share one word.
branches.cn: 个人帮助与公共系统共用一个词。

intro.en: Service belongs to the Latin servus family of service and duty.
intro.cn: service 属于拉丁语 servus（奴仆）词族，关联服务与职责。

latinIntro.en: Latin servitium and servus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 servitium 与 servus 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 这家公司提供许多服务。

items.example: The old bike is still serviceable.
That advice did him a disservice.
items.exampleCN: 那条建议帮了他的倒忙。

definition_zh: 放置；设置；树立；凝固；一套
definition_en: to put something in place, to adjust equipment, to establish something, to become solid, or a group of things used together
core_image: 闹钟被放到床头，指针停在六点
scene: 她把花瓶放在桌上。She set the vase on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 set 是「放置」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把花瓶放在桌上。

senses.title: To place
senses.definition: to put something in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到特定位置
senses.example: She set the vase on the table.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To adjust
senses.definition: to adjust a device or arrange something in advance
senses.definitionCN: 调整装置或预先安排好
senses.example: He set the alarm for six.
senses.why: Setting a device is placing its state.
senses.whyCN: 设置装置就是安放它的状态。

senses.title: To establish
senses.definition: to establish a record, rule, or example
senses.definitionCN: 创下纪录、定下规则或树立榜样
senses.example: The team set a new record.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍创下了新纪录。
senses.why: An idea can be placed firmly too.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能被牢牢安放。

senses.title: To become solid
senses.definition: to become solid or fixed
senses.definitionCN: 变成固体或固定下来
senses.example: The jelly will set in the fridge.
senses.why: A liquid takes a fixed shape.
senses.whyCN: 液体固定成一种形状。

senses.title: A group of things
senses.definition: a group of things that belong together
senses.definitionCN: 配套的一组东西
senses.example: She bought a set of tools.
senses.why: The noun names things placed together.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set comes from Old English settan, to cause to sit, from the same root as sit.
intro.cn: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），与 sit 同根。

items.en: Satjan meant to cause to sit.
items.cn: satjan 意为使坐下。

items.en: Settan meant to place or set.
items.cn: settan 意为放置、安放。

items.en: Set kept its placing sense.
items.cn: set 保留了放置的含义。

items.en: Set extended to devices and records.
items.cn: set 扩展到装置设置与纪录。

items.en: The noun named a matched group.
items.cn: 名词形式指配套的一组。

note.en: Set is compared with similar-looking words and with words for placing.
note.cn: 把 set 与形近词以及表示放置的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Set is the act of causing something to sit: an object, a clock, a record, or a liquid.
normalIntro.cn: set 就是让某物「坐下」：一个物件、一只钟、一项纪录或一种液体。

normal.en: Set the cup on the shelf.
Set the alarm before bed.
They set a record in the relay.
normal.cn: 他们在接力赛中创下纪录。

normal.en: Leave the cement to set.
This set of dishes has six plates.
normal.cn: 这套餐具共有六个盘子。

abstract.en: To set something is to decide where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 安放某物，就是决定它该在哪里。

abstract.en: A record is a moment set into history.
abstract.cn: 纪录，是被安放进历史的一刻。

abstract.en: Some things set only when we stop holding them.
abstract.cn: 有些东西，只有我们松手后才会定型。

examples.en: She set the vase on the table.
He set the alarm for six.
The jelly will set in the fridge.

dict_mnemonic.text: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），核心义「把东西安放到某个位置」，引申出设置、树立、凝固与一套。

root: 源自古英语 settan（使坐下、安放），与 sit 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Set means to place, adjust, establish, become solid, or a matched group.
sensesIntro.cn: set 意为放置、设置、树立、凝固或一套。

core.en: Causing something to take a fixed place.
core.cn: 使某物占据一个固定的位置。

branches.en: Putting an object down.
Arranging a device.
Fixing a record or rule.
A liquid taking shape.
Things placed together.
branches.cn: 被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set is a short native verb that joins with prefixes to make many new words.
intro.cn: set 是简短的日耳曼语本族动词，能与前缀组合出许多新词。

latinIntro.en: Set has no Latin ancestor; Latin ponere, to place, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: set 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ponere（放置）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She sets the table every night.
The story has a rural setting.
The oven is preset to 180 degrees.
items.exampleCN: 烤箱预设为一百八十度。

items.example: Reset the clock after the power cut.

items.meaning: to balance one effect with another
items.exampleCN: 节省抵消了更高的成本。

items.example: The setter placed the ball well.

definition_en: the number 7, a group of seven things, or the age of seven
core_image: 日历上七个方格排成一排，正好是一周
scene: 一周有七天。There are seven days in a week.
sceneCN: 这里 seven 是「七」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一周有七天。

senses.title: The number seven
senses.definition: the number equal to six plus one
senses.definitionCN: 等于六加一的数字
senses.example: There are seven days in a week.
senses.why: This is the basic counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的计数义项。

senses.title: A group of seven
senses.definition: a set or group of seven things or people
senses.definitionCN: 由七个事物或人组成的一组
senses.example: The choir sang in sevens.
senses.why: Numbers also name groups.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能命名成组的单位。

senses.title: Age seven
senses.definition: the age of seven years
senses.definitionCN: 七岁的年龄
senses.example: He learned to swim at seven.
senses.why: A number can mark a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能标记人生的阶段。

intro.en: Seven goes back to Proto-Germanic sebun and further to an ancient root septm.
intro.cn: seven 上溯至原始日耳曼语 sebun，更早来自表示「七」的古老词根 septm。

items.en: Septm meant seven.
items.cn: septm 意为七。

items.en: Sebun meant seven.
items.cn: sebun 意为七。

items.en: Seofon meant seven.
items.cn: seofon 意为七。

items.en: Seven took its modern form.
items.cn: seven 形成现代拼写。

items.en: Seven also named groups and ages.
items.cn: seven 也用来指成组数量与年龄。

note.en: Seven is compared with similar-looking words and with other number words.
note.cn: 把 seven 与形近词以及其他数词作比较。

entries.definition: more than two but not many

normalIntro.en: Seven fills a week and often carries a sense of completeness.
normalIntro.cn: seven 填满一周，常常带着一种完整感。

normal.en: A week has seven days.
The shop opens at seven.
She has seven brothers.
The seventh day was sunny.
They counted the coins in sevens.
normal.cn: 他们把硬币七个一组地数。

abstract.en: Seven gathers the days into a single week.
abstract.cn: 七，把日子收拢成一个星期。

abstract.en: Some numbers feel complete before we can explain why.
abstract.cn: 有些数字在我们能解释之前，就已显得完整。

abstract.en: Counting is a way of making time visible.
abstract.cn: 计数，是让时间变得可见的一种方式。

examples.en: There are seven days in a week.
He learned to swim at seven.
The choir sang in sevens.

dict_mnemonic.text: seven 来自古英语 seofon，与德语 sieben、拉丁语 septem 同源，核心义就是数字「七」。

root: 源自古英语 seofon（七），与拉丁语 septem 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Seven means the number 7, a group of seven, or the age of seven.
sensesIntro.cn: seven 意为数字七、七个一组或七岁。

core.en: The count that fills a week.
core.cn: 填满一周的那个数。

branches.en: The number itself.
A set of seven things.
branches.cn: 由七个事物组成的一组。

branches.en: The seventh year of life.
Number and group share one form.
branches.cn: 数字与成组共用一个形式。

branches.en: Counting years is still counting.

intro.en: Seven is a native Germanic number word that builds a whole family of numbers.
intro.cn: seven 是日耳曼语本族数词，能构成一整族数字词。

latinIntro.en: Seven has no Latin ancestor; Latin septem, seven, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: seven 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 septem（七）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 把纸牌按七张一组分开。

items.example: This is his seventh year here.
items.exampleCN: 这是他在这里的第七年。

items.example: They held a seventieth birthday party.
items.exampleCN: 他们举办了七十岁生日会。

definition_en: the number 17, a group of seventeen things, or the age of seventeen
core_image: 生日蛋糕上插着十七根蜡烛，火苗排成一圈
scene: 班上有十七名学生。There are seventeen students in the class.
sceneCN: 这里 seventeen 是「十七」（第 1 个义项）；句意：班上有十七名学生。

senses.title: The number seventeen
senses.definition: the number equal to sixteen plus one
senses.definitionCN: 等于十六加一的数字
senses.example: There are seventeen students in the class.
senses.why: This is the basic counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的计数义项。

senses.title: A group of seventeen
senses.definition: a set or group of seventeen things or people
senses.definitionCN: 由十七个事物或人组成的一组
senses.example: Seventeen were chosen for the team.
senses.why: Numbers also name groups.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能命名成组的单位。

senses.title: Age seventeen
senses.definition: the age of seventeen years
senses.definitionCN: 十七岁的年龄
senses.example: She moved to the city at seventeen.
senses.exampleCN: 她十七岁时搬到了城里。
senses.why: A number can mark a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能标记人生的阶段。

intro.en: Seventeen is seven plus the old suffix -teen, which means ten more.
intro.cn: seventeen 是 seven 加上古老后缀 -teen（再加十）构成。

items.en: Seofon meant seven.
items.cn: seofon 意为七。

items.en: Seofontiene meant seventeen.
items.cn: seofontiene 意为十七。

items.en: Seventene took a simpler form.
items.cn: seventene 形成更简的形式。

items.en: Seventeen settled its modern spelling.
items.cn: seventeen 固定了现代拼写。

items.en: Seventeen also named groups and ages.
items.cn: seventeen 也用来指成组数量与年龄。

note.en: Seventeen is compared with similar-looking words and with other number words.

He turned seventeen in May.
The seventeenth caller won a prize.

abstract.en: Seventeen stands at the edge of childhood.

abstract.en: A number can hold a whole year of waiting.

abstract.en: Counting years is counting changes.

definition_en: coming after the sixth, or one of seven equal parts
core_image: 赛道旁的计分牌停在数字七，名次栏写着第七
scene: 她在比赛中获得第七名。She finished seventh in the race.
sceneCN: 这里 seventh 是「第七」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在比赛中获得第七名。

senses.title: The seventh in order

senses.definitionCN: 在一系列中排在第六之后的
senses.example: She finished seventh in the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她在比赛中获得第七名。
senses.why: This is the ordinal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是序数义项。

senses.title: One of seven parts
senses.definition: one of seven equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被均分为七份中的一份
senses.example: A seventh of the cake was left.
senses.why: Ordinals also name fractions.

items.en: Seofon meant seven.

items.en: Seofotha meant seventh.
items.cn: seofotha 意为第七。

items.en: Seventhe took a clearer form.

items.en: Seventh settled its modern spelling.
items.cn: seventh 固定了现代拼写。

items.en: Seventh also named a fraction.
items.cn: seventh 也用来表示分数。

normalIntro.en: Seventh marks the place after six and also one slice out of seven.
normalIntro.cn: seventh 既标记六之后的位置，也指七份中的一份。

normal.en: He lives on the seventh floor.
She came seventh in the final.
The seventh day was a holiday.
Only a seventh of the land is farmed.
normal.cn: 只有七分之一的土地被耕种。

normal.en: He is in the seventh grade.

abstract.en: An ordinal turns a count into a position.
abstract.cn: 序数词把数量变成了位置。

abstract.en: Seven parts can make one whole, and one part can still matter.
abstract.cn: 七份能合成一个整体，而一份也仍然重要。

abstract.en: The seventh step is still a step forward.
abstract.cn: 第七步，依然是向前的一步。

examples.en: She finished seventh in the race.
examples.cn: 她在比赛中获得第七名。

examples.en: A seventh of the cake was left.
He lives on the seventh floor.

sensesIntro.en: Seventh means coming after the sixth or one of seven equal parts.
sensesIntro.cn: seventh 意为第七或七分之一。

Order and fraction share the suffix.

A share of a whole.

definition_en: the number 70, a group of seventy things, or the age of seventy
core_image: 一本旧相册摊开，页码停在第70页
scene: 这座桥有七十年的历史。The bridge is seventy years old.
sceneCN: 这里 seventy 是「七十」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座桥有七十年的历史。

senses.title: The number seventy
senses.definition: the number equal to seven times ten
senses.definitionCN: 等于七乘十的数字
senses.example: The bridge is seventy years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥有七十年的历史。
senses.why: This is the basic counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的计数义项。

senses.title: A group of seventy
senses.definition: a set or group of seventy things or people
senses.definitionCN: 由七十个事物或人组成的一组
senses.example: Seventy were invited to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 有七十人被邀请参加晚宴。
senses.why: Numbers also name groups.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能命名成组的单位。

senses.title: Age seventy
senses.definition: the age of seventy years
senses.definitionCN: 七十岁的年龄
senses.example: She still paints at seventy.
senses.why: A number can mark a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能标记人生的阶段。

intro.en: Seventy is seven plus the old suffix -ty, meaning a group of ten.
intro.cn: seventy 是 seven 加古老后缀 -ty（十的倍数）构成。

items.en: Seofon meant seven.
items.cn: seofon 意为七。

items.en: Seofontig meant seventy.
items.cn: seofontig 意为七十。

items.en: Seventi took a simpler form.
items.cn: seventi 形成更简的形式。

items.en: Seventy settled its modern spelling.
items.cn: seventy 固定了现代拼写。

items.en: Seventy also named groups and ages.
items.cn: seventy 也用来指成组数量与年龄。

note.en: Seventy is compared with similar-looking words and with other tens.
note.cn: 把 seventy 与形近词以及其他整十数词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Seventy is seven tens, a number often linked to long experience.
normalIntro.cn: seventy 是七个十，常与漫长的经历联系在一起。

normal.en: The old tree is seventy years old.
Seventy people filled the hall.
He is in his seventies.
The temperature reached seventy degrees.
The seventieth guest arrived last.

abstract.en: Seventy years can wear stone into soft curves.
abstract.cn: 七十年，能把石头磨出柔和的曲线。

abstract.en: A lifetime is a number we can only count backward.
abstract.cn: 一生是我们只能倒着数的数字。

abstract.en: Age is a measure, not a limit.
abstract.cn: 年龄是一种尺度，而不是界限。

examples.en: The bridge is seventy years old.
examples.cn: 这座桥有七十年的历史。

examples.en: Seventy were invited to the dinner.
examples.cn: 有七十人被邀请参加晚宴。

examples.en: She still paints at seventy.

root: 由古英语 seofon（七）加 -tig（十的倍数）演变而来。

sensesIntro.en: Seventy means the number 70, a group of seventy, or the age of seventy.

core.cn: 七个十。

branches.en: The number itself.
A set of seventy things.

Number and group share one form.

intro.cn: seventy 把 seven 与表示十的倍数的后缀 -ty 连接起来。

latinIntro.en: Seventy has no Latin ancestor; Latin septuaginta is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: seventy 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 septuaginta（七十）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The building dates from the seventies.

items.exampleCN: 人们庆祝了他们的第七十年。
这是一个七十年的传统。

definition_en: more than two but not many, or separate and individual
core_image: 门口站着几个人，彼此隔开一小段距离
scene: 有几个人在外面等候。Several people waited outside.
sceneCN: 这里 several 是「几个」（第 1 个义项）；句意：有几个人在外面等候。

senses.title: More than two but not many
senses.definition: more than two but not a large number
senses.definitionCN: 多于两个但数量不大
senses.example: Several people waited outside.
senses.why: This is the everyday quantity sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的数量义项。

senses.title: Separate and individual
senses.definition: separate or different from one another
senses.definitionCN: 彼此分开或各不相同的
senses.example: They returned to their several homes.
senses.why: The older sense stresses separation.
senses.whyCN: 较早的义项强调彼此分开。

intro.en: Several comes from Anglo-French several, from Medieval Latin separalis, from separ, separate.
intro.cn: several 来自盎格鲁法语 several，上溯至中世纪拉丁语 separalis，源自 separ（分开的）。

items.en: Separ meant separate or distinct.
items.cn: separ 意为分开的、各别的。

items.en: Separalis meant relating to separate things.
items.cn: separalis 意为与各别事物相关的。

items.en: Several meant distinct or different.
items.cn: several 意为各别的、不同的。

items.en: Several meant separate or individual.
items.cn: several 意为分开的或各自的。

items.en: Several came to mean a small number.
items.cn: several 逐渐指不大的数量。

note.en: Several is compared with similar-looking words and with words for an unspecified number.
note.cn: 把 several 与形近词以及表示不确定数量的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Several is a small, separate group of things, more than a couple but not a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: several 是一小群彼此分开的事物，比两三个多，但还算不上人群。

normal.en: Several cars were parked outside.
I have read the book several times.
Several of the windows were open.
They tried several ways to fix it.
normal.cn: 他们试了几种办法来修它。

normal.en: Several years passed before they met again.
normal.cn: 过了几年他们才再次相见。

abstract.en: Several keeps things distinct even while counting them together.
abstract.cn: several 在把事物一起清点的同时，仍让它们彼此分明。

abstract.en: A few is enough to change a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 几个人，就足以改变一个安静的房间。

abstract.en: The exact number matters less than the fact of company.
abstract.cn: 确切的数量，不如有人在场这件事重要。

examples.en: Several people waited outside.
Several of the books were old.
They returned to their several homes.

dict_mnemonic.text: several 源自拉丁语 separ（分开的），核心义「各自分开的」，后引申为「几个」。

root: 源自拉丁语 separ（分开的），经中世纪拉丁语 separalis 与盎格鲁法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.cn: several 意为几个或各自的。

core.en: A small set of distinct things.
core.cn: 一小群彼此分明的事物。

branches.en: A small number of things.
Things that are separate.
The number keeps the items distinct.
branches.cn: 这个数量词仍让各项彼此分明。

branches.en: More than a pair, less than a crowd.
Each one goes its own way.

intro.en: Several belongs to the Latin separ- family of separation.
intro.cn: several 属于拉丁语 separ-（分开）词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin separ, separate, also gave separate, sever, and severance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 separ（分开的）也孕育了 separate、sever 与 severance。

items.example: The land is held in severalty.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地由各人分别所有。

items.example: Sever the rope with a knife.
The severance of the link was final.

definition_zh: 摇动；动摇；发抖；握手；奶昔
definition_en: to move quickly from side to side, to make someone uncertain, to tremble, to hold hands in greeting, or a thick milk drink
core_image: 瓶子在手中上下晃动，里面的液体撞出细响
scene: 她打开瓶子前摇了摇。She shook the bottle before opening it.
sceneCN: 这里 shake 是「摇动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她打开瓶子前摇了摇。

senses.title: To move quickly
senses.definition: to move something quickly up and down or side to side
senses.definitionCN: 使某物快速上下或左右移动
senses.example: She shook the bottle before opening it.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To weaken confidence
senses.definition: to make someone feel uncertain or upset
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到不确定或不安
senses.example: The news shook her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息动摇了她的信心。
senses.why: A shock can shake the mind.
senses.whyCN: 冲击能摇动内心。

senses.title: To tremble
senses.definition: to tremble with cold, fear, or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷、恐惧或情绪而颤抖
senses.example: He shook with cold.
senses.why: The body shakes when it loses steadiness.
senses.whyCN: 身体失去稳定时就会发抖。

senses.title: To greet with hands
senses.definition: to hold and move someone's hand as a greeting
senses.definitionCN: 以握住并摇动对方的手来表示问候
senses.example: They shook hands at the door.
senses.why: The gesture moves the joined hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势让相握的手摇动。

senses.title: Milk drink
senses.definition: a thick drink of milk and ice cream
senses.definitionCN: 由牛奶和冰淇淋摇匀的浓稠饮料
senses.example: He ordered a chocolate shake.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯巧克力奶昔。
senses.why: The drink is shaken before serving.
senses.whyCN: 这种饮料在供应前要摇匀。

intro.en: Shake comes from Old English sceacan, to move with a quick back-and-forth motion.
intro.cn: shake 源自古英语 sceacan，意为快速来回移动。

items.en: Skakan meant to shake.
items.cn: skakan 意为摇动。

items.en: Sceacan meant to move quickly.
items.cn: sceacan 意为快速移动。

items.en: Shake kept the same motion.
items.cn: shake 保留了同样的动作。

items.en: Shake named a greeting with hands.
items.cn: shake 指握手的问候。

items.en: Shake named a thick milk drink.
items.cn: shake 指浓稠的奶制饮料。

note.en: Shake is compared with similar-looking words and with words for trembling and moving.
note.cn: 把 shake 与形近词以及表示颤抖和移动的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move rapidly back and forth

normalIntro.en: Shake moves from the bottle to the voice, the body, the hand, and the glass.
normalIntro.cn: shake 从瓶子一路摇到声音、身体、手和杯子。

normal.en: Shake the juice before drinking.
The bad news shook the whole team.
normal.cn: 坏消息震动了整个团队。

normal.en: She was shaking with fear.
They shook hands and smiled.
He drank a strawberry shake.

abstract.en: To shake is to interrupt steadiness for a moment.
abstract.cn: 摇动，就是短暂地打断稳定。

abstract.en: A handshake can carry more truth than a speech.
abstract.cn: 一次握手，可能比一段话更真实。

abstract.en: What shakes us also shows what holds us.
abstract.cn: 摇动我们的东西，也显出我们被什么托住。

examples.en: She shook the bottle before opening it.
The news shook her confidence.
examples.cn: 这个消息动摇了她的信心。

examples.en: They shook hands at the door.

dict_mnemonic.text: shake 源自古英语 sceacan（摇动），核心义「来回快速移动」，引申出动摇、发抖与握手。

root: 源自古英语 sceacan（摇动），与德语 schütteln 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shake means to move quickly, to weaken confidence, to tremble, to greet with hands, or a milk drink.
sensesIntro.cn: shake 意为摇动、动摇、发抖、握手或奶昔。

core.en: A quick back-and-forth movement.
core.cn: 快速的来回移动。

branches.en: Moving an object quickly.
Moving confidence off balance.
A body that cannot stay still.
Two hands moving together.
A drink that was shaken.

intro.en: Shake is a strong native verb with irregular past forms.
intro.cn: shake 是日耳曼语本族强变化动词，过去式不规则。

latinIntro.en: Shake has no Latin ancestor; Latin quatere, to shake, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shake 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 quatere（摇动）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He was shaken by the news.
She filled the shaker with ice.

items.exampleCN: 有力的握手能建立信任。

definition_en: used with I or we for the future, used in rules to mean must, or used to make an offer or suggestion
core_image: 电话听筒贴在耳边，明天的那通电话还没有拨出
scene: 我明天会给你打电话。I shall call you tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 shall 是「将」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我明天会给你打电话。

senses.title: Future with I or we
senses.definition: used with I or we to talk about the future
senses.definitionCN: 与 I 或 we 连用，表示将来
senses.example: I shall call you tomorrow.
senses.why: This is the traditional future use.
senses.whyCN: 这是传统的将来时用法。

senses.title: Must in rules
senses.definition: used in official rules to mean must
senses.definitionCN: 在正式规定中表示「必须」
senses.example: Students shall not smoke on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 学生不得在校园内吸烟。
senses.why: Law and rules use shall for obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律与规章用 shall 表示义务。

senses.title: Offer or suggestion
senses.definition: used in questions to offer something or suggest an action
senses.definitionCN: 在疑问句中用于提供某物或建议行动
senses.example: Shall we go for a walk?
senses.why: The question asks for agreement.
senses.whyCN: 这种疑问句在征求同意。

intro.en: Shall comes from Old English sceal, meaning owe or must, and softened into a future marker.
intro.cn: shall 源自古英语 sceal（欠、必须），后来弱化为将来时的标记。

items.en: Skal meant I owe or I must.
items.cn: skal 意为「我欠」或「我必须」。

items.en: Sceal meant must or ought.
items.cn: sceal 意为必须或应当。

items.en: Shall marked duty and future.
items.cn: shall 同时标记义务与将来。

items.en: Shall became a future helper with I and we.
items.cn: shall 成为与 I、we 连用的将来助动词。

items.en: Rules kept shall for obligation.
items.cn: 规章保留了 shall 的义务含义。

note.en: Shall is compared with similar-looking words and with other modal verbs.
note.cn: 把 shall 与形近词以及其他情态动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shall began as a word for owing and became a gentle way to mark the future or a rule.
normalIntro.cn: shall 最初表示「欠」，后来变成标记将来或规定的温和方式。

normal.en: I shall see you next week.
We shall need more time.
The rule says visitors shall sign in.
Shall I open the window?
Shall we begin?

abstract.en: A word of obligation can soften into a word of invitation.
abstract.cn: 一个表示义务的词，也能软化成邀请。

abstract.en: The future is often spoken as a promise.
abstract.cn: 将来，常常是被当作承诺说出来的。

abstract.en: Rules sound gentler when they use an old, quiet word.
abstract.cn: 用上一个古老而安静的词，规定也会显得温和。

examples.en: I shall call you tomorrow.
Students shall not smoke on campus.
examples.cn: 学生不得在校园内吸烟。

examples.en: Shall we go for a walk?

root: 源自古英语 sceal（欠、必须），与 should 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shall marks the future with I or we, obligation in rules, or a polite offer.
sensesIntro.cn: shall 表示与 I、we 连用的将来、规章中的义务或礼貌的提议。

core.en: A modal word that moves from owing to intending.
core.cn: 从「欠」走向「打算」的情态词。

branches.en: A future spoken with I or we.
branches.cn: 与 I 或 we 连用的将来。

branches.en: An obligation written in rules.
A question that offers or suggests.
Promise and duty share one form.
branches.cn: 承诺与义务共用一个形式。

branches.en: The same word can command or invite.
branches.cn: 同一个词既能命令，也能邀请。

intro.en: Shall belongs to the old Germanic modal verbs, with should as its past form.
intro.cn: shall 属于古老的日耳曼语情态动词，should 是它的过去式形式。

latinIntro.en: Shall has no Latin ancestor; Latin debere, to owe, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shall 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 debere（欠、应当）只是语义对应词。

definition_en: a painful feeling of having done wrong, a cause of disgrace, or to make someone feel ashamed
core_image: 被当众指出错误，脸一下子烧起来
scene: 他因说谎而感到羞愧。He felt shame for lying.
sceneCN: 这里 shame 是「羞愧」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他因说谎而感到羞愧。

senses.title: Painful feeling
senses.definition: a painful feeling caused by knowing you did wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因知道自己做错而感到的痛苦
senses.example: He felt shame for lying.
senses.why: This is the central emotional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的情感义项。

senses.title: Disgrace
senses.definition: loss of honour or respect
senses.definitionCN: 荣誉或尊重的丧失
senses.example: The scandal brought shame on the family.
senses.why: Shame can be a public state, not only a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 羞耻可以是公开的状态，而不只是私人感受。

senses.title: To make ashamed
senses.definition: to make someone feel shame
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到羞愧
senses.example: She was shamed by his words.
senses.why: The noun became a verb of causing the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为引起这种感觉的动词。

senses.title: A pity
senses.definition: something unfortunate, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 不幸的事，用于口语
senses.example: It is a shame you cannot come.
senses.why: A mild regret is softened by the word shame.
senses.whyCN: 轻微的遗憾用 shame 来缓和。

intro.en: Shame comes from Old English sceamu, a Germanic word for the feeling of disgrace.
intro.cn: shame 源自古英语 sceamu，是日耳曼语中表示羞耻感的词。

items.en: The root named a sense of disgrace.
items.cn: 这个词根指羞耻感。

items.en: Sceamu meant shame or modesty.
items.cn: sceamu 意为羞耻或谦逊。

items.en: Shame named both feeling and disgrace.
items.cn: shame 既指感受也指耻辱。

items.en: The verb meant to bring shame on someone.
items.cn: 动词形式意为使某人蒙羞。

items.en: The phrase a shame came to mean a pity.
items.cn: 短语 a shame 开始表示可惜。

note.en: Shame is compared with similar-looking words and with words for disgrace.
note.cn: 把 shame 与形近词以及表示耻辱的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shame is the heat of being seen doing wrong, and the social mark it leaves.
normalIntro.cn: shame 是被看见做错事时的灼热感，以及它留下的社会印记。

normal.en: He hung his head in shame.
The lie brought shame on him.
It is a shame she left early.
Shame can stop people from repeating mistakes.
normal.cn: 羞耻能阻止人们重犯错误。

normal.en: He was shamed into apologising.

abstract.en: Shame is a mirror held by other people.
abstract.cn: 羞耻是别人举起的镜子。

abstract.en: Too much shame can teach the wrong lesson.
abstract.cn: 过多的羞耻可能教错道理。

abstract.en: A pity and a disgrace share one small word.
abstract.cn: 可惜与耻辱共用一个不起眼的词。

examples.en: He felt shame for lying.
The scandal brought shame on the family.
It is a shame you cannot come.

dict_mnemonic.text: shame 源自古英语 sceamu（羞耻），核心义「被看见做错时的痛苦」，由私人感受引申为公开耻辱与可惜。

root: 源自古英语 sceamu（羞耻、谦逊），核心义「做错事后被看见的痛苦」。

sensesIntro.en: Shame means the pain of wrongdoing, public disgrace, to make someone ashamed, or a pity.
sensesIntro.cn: shame 意为做错事的痛苦、公开耻辱、使某人羞愧或憾事。

core.en: The pain of being seen as wrong.
core.cn: 被看作做错事时的痛苦。

branches.en: A burning private feeling.
A public loss of honour.
The act of making another feel it.
branches.cn: 使他人产生这种感觉的行为。

branches.en: A softened word for regret.
Private pain and public disgrace share one word.
branches.cn: 私人痛苦与公开耻辱共用一个词。

intro.en: Shame builds words for the presence or absence of shame.
intro.cn: shame 构成表示有羞耻或无羞耻的词。

latinIntro.en: Shame has no Latin ancestor; Latin pudor, a sense of shame, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shame 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pudor（羞耻感）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She felt shamed by the comment.

items.exampleCN: 无耻的谎言让我们震惊。

definition_en: the outer form of something, to give something a form, or the condition of something
core_image: 双手把湿泥捏成一只碗的弧线
scene: 云朵慢慢变成了船的形状。The cloud slowly took the shape of a boat.
sceneCN: 这里 shape 是「形状」（第 1 个义项）；句意：云朵慢慢变成了船的形状。

senses.title: Outer form
senses.definition: the outline or form of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的外轮廓或形态
senses.example: The cloud slowly took the shape of a boat.
senses.exampleCN: 云朵慢慢变成了船的形状。
senses.why: This is the basic visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的视觉义项。

senses.title: To form
senses.definition: to give something a particular form
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某物特定的形态
senses.example: She shaped the clay into a bowl.
senses.why: The noun became a verb of forming.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为成形的动词。

senses.title: Condition
senses.definition: the state of something, especially health
senses.definitionCN: 某物的状态，尤指健康
senses.example: He is in good shape this year.
senses.why: The body's form reflects its condition.
senses.whyCN: 身体的外形反映其状况。

senses.title: Influence
senses.definition: to influence how something develops
senses.definitionCN: 影响某事物如何发展
senses.example: Early years shape character.
senses.why: Shaping is not only physical but also mental.
senses.whyCN: 塑造不仅是物理的，也是心理的。

intro.en: Shape comes from Old English gesceap, creation or form, from the verb sceppan, to create.
intro.cn: shape 源自古英语 gesceap（创造、形态），来自动词 sceppan（创造）。

items.en: The root meant to create or shape.
items.cn: 这个词根意为创造或塑造。

items.en: Sceppan meant to create.
items.cn: sceppan 意为创造。

items.en: Gesceap meant a created form.
items.cn: gesceap 意为被创造的形态。

items.en: Shape named the outline of a thing.
items.cn: shape 指事物的外轮廓。

items.en: The verb meant to form or influence.
items.cn: 动词形式意为塑造或影响形成。

note.en: Shape is compared with similar-looking words and with words for form and outline.
note.cn: 把 shape 与形近词以及表示形态和轮廓的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shape is an outline you can see, a form you can make, and the condition that form is in.
normalIntro.cn: shape 是看得见的轮廓、能做出的形态，以及形态所处的状况。

normal.en: The table has a round shape.
Clay can be shaped by hand.
The plan is taking shape.
Exercise keeps you in shape.
Childhood shapes the adult.

abstract.en: A shape is a boundary the eye can hold.
abstract.cn: 形状是眼睛能把握的边界。

abstract.en: To shape is to leave a mark on what will grow.
abstract.cn: 塑造就是在将要生长之物上留下印记。

abstract.en: Condition is a shape you cannot see.
abstract.cn: 状况是你看不见的形状。

examples.en: The cloud slowly took the shape of a boat.
examples.cn: 云朵慢慢变成了船的形状。

examples.en: She shaped the clay into a bowl.
He is in good shape this year.

dict_mnemonic.text: shape 源自古英语 gesceap（创造出的形态），核心义「被造出的轮廓」，由形状引申为塑造与状况。

root: 源自古英语 gesceap（创造、形态），核心义「被造出的外轮廓」。

sensesIntro.en: Shape means an outer form, to form something, a condition, or to influence development.
sensesIntro.cn: shape 意为形状、塑造、状况或影响形成。

core.en: An outline that holds a thing together.
core.cn: 把事物组织起来的外轮廓。

branches.en: The visible outline of a thing.
The act of giving form.
The state a body is in.
Influence on how something grows.
branches.cn: 对某物如何生长的影响。

branches.en: The form and the forming share one word.
branches.cn: 形态与塑形共用一个词。

intro.en: Shape builds words for forms, their absence, and their beauty.
intro.cn: shape 构成表示形态、形态缺失和形态之美的词。

latinIntro.en: Shape has no Latin ancestor; Latin forma, form, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shape 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 forma（形状）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The tiles come in many shapes.
The handle is shaped like a hook.

items.exampleCN: 他穿着一件没有形的外套。

items.example: The vase has a shapely neck.

definition_en: to give part of something to others, to use something together, a portion of something, or a unit of ownership in a company
core_image: 一块饼被切开，每人手里拿到相同的一角
scene: 她把蛋糕分给每个孩子。She shared the cake with every child.
sceneCN: 这里 share 是「分享」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把蛋糕分给每个孩子。

senses.title: Give a part
senses.definition: to give part of something to other people
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的一部分给别人
senses.example: She shared the cake with every child.
senses.exampleCN: 她把蛋糕分给每个孩子。
senses.why: This is the everyday social sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常社交义项。

senses.title: Use together
senses.definition: to use something with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起使用某物
senses.example: They share a small office.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合用一间小办公室。
senses.why: Sharing can mean joint use rather than division.
senses.whyCN: 分享也可以指共同使用而非分割。

senses.title: Portion
senses.definition: a part of something that belongs to one person
senses.definitionCN: 某物中属于某个人的部分
senses.example: Everyone got a fair share.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都得到公平的一份。
senses.why: The act of dividing produces shares.
senses.whyCN: 分割的行为产生了份额。

senses.title: Company stock
senses.definition: one of the equal parts of a company's ownership
senses.definitionCN: 公司所有权中均等的一份
senses.example: He bought shares in the company.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了这家公司的股份。
senses.why: Ownership is divided into shares like a cake.
senses.whyCN: 所有权像蛋糕一样被分成份额。

intro.en: Share comes from Old English scearu, a cutting or division, related to shear.
intro.cn: share 源自古英语 scearu（切分、份额），与 shear（剪）相关。

items.en: The root meant to cut or divide.
items.cn: 这个词根意为切或分。

items.en: Scearu meant a division or portion.
items.cn: scearu 意为分割或份额。

items.en: Share named a part given to someone.
items.cn: share 指分给某人的一份。

items.en: The verb meant to divide among people.
items.cn: 动词形式意为在人们之间分配。

items.en: Share named a unit of company ownership.
items.cn: share 指公司所有权的一份。

note.en: Share is compared with similar-looking words and with words for dividing.
note.cn: 把 share 与形近词以及表示分配的词作比较。

entries.definition: to cut wool from a sheep

normalIntro.en: To share is to cut a whole into parts and let others hold them.
normalIntro.cn: share 就是把整体切成部分，让别人也拿着。

normal.en: Share the umbrella with me.
They share the same birthday.
Each child had a share of the pie.
normal.cn: 每个孩子都分到一份派。

normal.en: She owns shares in a bank.
We share the work fairly.

abstract.en: A share is a piece of a whole that stays connected.
abstract.cn: 份额是整体中仍相连的一块。

abstract.en: Sharing makes one thing serve many.
abstract.cn: 分享让一样东西服务许多人。

abstract.en: Fair division is harder than cutting.
abstract.cn: 公平分配比切割更难。

examples.en: She shared the cake with every child.
examples.cn: 她把蛋糕分给每个孩子。

examples.en: They share a small office.
examples.cn: 他们合用一间小办公室。

examples.en: He bought shares in the company.
examples.cn: 他买了这家公司的股份。

dict_mnemonic.text: share 源自古英语 scearu（切分、份额），核心义「切开后的一份」，由分配引申为合用与股份。

root: 源自古英语 scearu（切分、份额），与 shear（剪）同源，核心义「分出来的一份」。

sensesIntro.en: Share means to give part away, to use together, a portion, or a unit of stock.
sensesIntro.cn: share 意为分给他人、合用、份额或股份。

core.en: A part cut from a whole.
core.cn: 从整体中切出的一份。

branches.en: Giving part of what you have.
Using one thing together.
The piece that belongs to one.
Ownership divided into units.
branches.cn: 被分成单位的公司所有权。

branches.en: The act and the portion share one word.
branches.cn: 分配动作与所得份额共用一个词。

intro.en: Share builds words for joint use, investors, and distribution.
intro.cn: share 构成表示共用、投资者和分配的词。

latinIntro.en: Share has no Latin ancestor; Latin pars, a part, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: share 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pars（部分）只是语义对应词。

definition_en: the pronoun used for a woman or girl already mentioned
core_image: 一位女性侧过身，长发在肩后划过
scene: 她明天会来。She will come tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 she 是「她」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她明天会来。

senses.title: Female person
senses.definition: the pronoun for a woman or girl already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 指代已提到的女性或女孩的代词
senses.example: She said she would come tomorrow.
senses.why: This is the basic grammatical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的语法义项。

senses.title: Female animal
senses.definition: the pronoun for a female animal
senses.definitionCN: 指代雌性动物的代词
senses.example: The mare is old; she still works.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹母马老了，她仍在干活。
senses.why: Animals with known sex are often called he or she.
senses.whyCN: 已知性别的动物常用 he 或 she。

senses.title: Ship or country
senses.definition: a traditional pronoun for ships, countries, or machines
senses.definitionCN: 传统上指代船只、国家或机器的代词
senses.example: The ship lost her mast.
senses.why: An old convention treats these as female.
senses.whyCN: 旧习惯把这些事物视为女性。

intro.en: She comes from Old English heo, the feminine subject pronoun.
intro.cn: she 源自古英语 heo，是阴性主格代词。

items.en: The root was the feminine subject pronoun.
items.cn: 这个词根是阴性主格代词。

items.en: Heo meant she.
items.cn: heo 意为她。

items.en: She replaced heo in northern dialects.
items.cn: she 在北部方言中取代了 heo。

items.en: She spread through standard English.
items.cn: she 传播到标准英语中。

items.en: She also names female animals and ships.
items.cn: she 也指雌性动物和船只。

note.en: She is compared with similar-looking words and with other pronouns.
note.cn: 把 she 与形近词以及其他代词作比较。

normalIntro.en: She points to one female person already in the sentence or the scene.
normalIntro.cn: she 指向句中或场景里已经出现的一位女性。

normal.en: She opened the door.
She is my sister.
I gave her the book.
The book is hers.
She made it herself.

abstract.en: A pronoun is a small hand pointing back.
abstract.cn: 代词是一只向后指的小手。

abstract.en: She carries a whole person in three letters.
abstract.cn: she 用三个字母承载一个人。

abstract.en: The word changes with the grammar, not the person.
abstract.cn: 这个词随语法变化，而不随人变化。

examples.en: She said she would come tomorrow.
The mare is old; she still works.
examples.cn: 那匹母马老了，她仍在干活。

examples.en: The ship lost her mast.

dict_mnemonic.text: she 源自古英语 heo（她），是英语最基本的阴性主格代词，另有宾格 her 与所有格 hers。

root: 源自古英语 heo（她），核心义「已提到的女性」。

sensesIntro.en: She is the subject pronoun for a woman, a female animal, or traditionally a ship.
sensesIntro.cn: she 是女性、雌性动物或传统上船只的主格代词。

core.en: A pointer to a female already named.
core.cn: 指向已提到的女性的标记。

branches.en: A woman or girl as subject.
branches.cn: 作为主语的女性或女孩。

branches.en: A female animal as subject.
A ship treated as female.
People and animals share the pronoun.
branches.cn: 人与动物共用这个代词。

branches.en: The female pronoun extends to things.

intro.en: She has a small set of related pronoun forms.
intro.cn: she 有一小组相关的代词形式。

latinIntro.en: She has no Latin ancestor; Latin ea, she, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: she 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ea（她）只是语义对应词。

definition_en: a farm animal kept for wool and meat, or a person who follows others without thinking
core_image: 一只绵羊低头啃草，厚厚的羊毛像一团云
scene: 羊群在草地上吃草。The sheep grazed on the grass.
sceneCN: 这里 sheep 是「绵羊」（第 1 个义项）；句意：羊群在草地上吃草。

senses.title: Farm animal
senses.definition: a farm animal with thick wool
senses.definitionCN: 长着厚羊毛的农场动物
senses.example: The sheep grazed on the grass.
senses.why: This is the basic animal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的动物义项。

senses.title: Wool source
senses.definition: the animal as a source of wool or meat
senses.definitionCN: 作为羊毛或肉来源的动物
senses.example: The farm keeps sheep for wool.
senses.why: The animal stands for the product it gives.
senses.whyCN: 动物代指它所提供的产品。

senses.title: Blind follower
senses.definition: a person who follows others without thinking
senses.definitionCN: 不加思考跟随他人的人
senses.example: He is no sheep; he questions everything.
senses.exampleCN: 他不是盲从者，什么都质疑。
senses.why: Sheep are known for moving as a flock.
senses.whyCN: 羊以成群跟从而出名。

intro.en: Sheep comes from Old English sceap, a word shared across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: sheep 源自古英语 sceap，是日耳曼语各语言共有的词。

items.en: Skap named the wool-bearing animal.
items.cn: skap 指长毛的动物。

items.en: Sceap meant sheep, singular or plural.
items.cn: sceap 单复数同形，意为绵羊。

items.en: Sheep kept the same unchanging plural.
items.cn: sheep 保持不变的复数形式。

items.en: Sheep named the animal and its wool.
items.cn: sheep 指这种动物及其羊毛。

items.en: The word became a metaphor for blind followers.
items.cn: 这个词成为盲从者的隐喻。

note.en: Sheep is compared with similar-looking words and with words for farm animals.
note.cn: 把 sheep 与形近词以及表示农场动物的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flat board for storing things

normalIntro.en: Sheep is the woolly animal that moves as a flock, and a name for people who do the same.
normalIntro.cn: sheep 是成群移动的毛茸茸动物，也指同样盲从的人。

normal.en: The sheep are in the field.
One sheep is black.
The sheep dog guards the flock.
Sheep provide wool and meat.
Do not be a sheep; think first.

abstract.en: A flock is safe and also easy to lead.
abstract.cn: 羊群既安全又容易被带领。

abstract.en: Wool grows by being cut.
abstract.cn: 羊毛因被剪而生长。

abstract.en: One black sheep marks the whole flock.
abstract.cn: 一只黑羊标记了整个羊群。

examples.en: The sheep grazed on the grass.
The farm keeps sheep for wool.
He is no sheep; he questions everything.
examples.cn: 他不是盲从者，什么都质疑。

dict_mnemonic.text: sheep 源自古英语 sceap（绵羊），单复数同形，核心义「成群的毛用动物」，比喻盲从者。

root: 源自古英语 sceap（绵羊），核心义「成群的长毛家畜」。

sensesIntro.en: Sheep means a wool-bearing farm animal or a person who follows blindly.
sensesIntro.cn: sheep 意为产毛的农场动物或盲从者。

core.en: A woolly animal that stays in a flock.
core.cn: 待在群体中的长毛动物。

branches.en: The animal itself.
The wool or meat it gives.
A person who follows like one.
Animal and follower share the image.
branches.cn: 动物与跟从者共享这个意象。

branches.en: The animal and its product share a name.

intro.en: Sheep builds words for herding, enclosures, and shy behaviour.
intro.cn: sheep 构成表示放牧、围栏和羞怯行为的词。

latinIntro.en: Sheep has no Latin ancestor; Latin ovis, sheep, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: sheep 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ovis（羊）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The sheepdog ran behind the flock.
The sheepfold is beside the barn.
The chair is covered with sheepskin.
